findings.title: METAR-locked path's recommended side can contradict the lock's own outcome, and the divergence gate is skipped there
findings.root_cause: Side selection is a bare `blended_prob > market_prob`, but a monotone-safe lock's probability is floored at 0.72 by _dynamic_lock_in_confidence while its true likelihood is ~99.9%. The understatement flips the side rather than merely under-betting.
findings.evidence: Monotone-safe YES lock, blended_prob=0.72 vs market 0.90 -> rec_side='no', entry_side_edge=(1-0.72)-(1-0.90)=+0.18. Independently reproduced end-to-end through analyze_trade by an opus reviewer on the OKC/SATX incident shape.
findings.financial_risk: Places a confidently-sized bet against an outcome the lock has already determined is settled.
findings.decision_required: Raise the confidence floor for monotone-safe locks / enforce side-agreement with the lock verdict / stop skipping the divergence gate. Not equivalent -- only side-agreement closes it by construction.

findings.title: _var_from_ticker_prefix returns None for KXHOLIDAYTMIN, so a daily-MINIMUM market is analysed as a daily-MAXIMUM one
findings.root_cause: The helper keys off the substrings HIGH/LOW; the KXHOLIDAYTMAX/TMIN family uses TMAX/TMIN naming and contains neither, so the `or "max"` fallback silently mislabels every TMIN market.
findings.evidence: _var_from_ticker_prefix('KXHOLIDAYTMIN') -> None; _daily_var_from_series('KXHOLIDAYTMIN') -> 'max'. batch-68 traced a third consumer: the mislabel reaches ensemble_member_scores as var='max' with a MINIMUM actual_temp, which get_dynamic_station_bias reads for the max cell.
findings.financial_risk: None today (0 open holiday markets, gated behind _holiday_temp_gates_active). Once the family trades, a ~20-30F sign-flipped sample enters the correction subtracted from every daily-HIGH forecast for that city.

findings.title: One shared 'kalshi_api_read' circuit breaker lets auth failures on private endpoints disable public market-data reads, removing stop-loss protection
findings.root_cause: kalshi_client.py:93 declares one breaker for all reads and _get() routes both auth=True and auth=False through it, so a credential/clock fault on private endpoints trips it for public ones.
findings.evidence: 2026-08-26 00:28 UTC cron: six 401s on /portfolio/{balance,positions} (header_timestamp_expired, 41.4s clock skew) -> 'Circuit kalshi_api_read OPEN after 5 failures' -> '[StopLoss] got a usable quote for 0/8 open position(s) ... effectively unprotected'. get_market() is unsigned and could not have 401'd.
findings.financial_risk: Every open position unprotected for the cycle; unrealized P&L reads 0.00 via the entry_price fallback, so no stop can fire. The same cascade under LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED leaves real positions unprotected.
findings.decision_required: Split public/authenticated breakers; exclude 401 from breaker counting; decide stop-loss behaviour when a position cannot be priced; add a startup clock-skew assertion.

findings.title: Nothing records per-day that a scan ran, so an outage and a fully-gated day are indistinguishable
findings.root_cause: No per-day scan record exists; the A12 funnel panel's own docstring claims a distinction the data cannot support.
findings.evidence: batch-64 landed 2026-08-25 08:46 UTC and its four forward-only writers produced nothing until 00:30 UTC the next day because no scan ran in between. Invisible for a full day, and it led a downstream session to conclude the writers were broken.
findings.financial_risk: None directly; delays detection of a dead cron.
findings.decision_required: Whether the record carries a reached-analysis count rather than a bare ran/did-not-run flag.

findings.title: batch-64's two forward-only tables have no retention sweep, and one grows ~50x faster than its migration comment estimated
findings.root_cause: purge_old_predictions covers predictions and outcomes only; a grep for DELETE against either new table finds nothing.
findings.evidence: Measured 2026-08-26: one cron cycle wrote 597 real ensemble_member_values rows (17-50 members each, ~0.3-1KB). orderbook_depth_snapshots still 0 -- it is written from the WS listener thread and needs live trading. predictions.db is ~47MB and cloud_backup pushes it after every run.
findings.financial_risk: None; backup cost and unbounded disk growth.
findings.decision_required: Retention window PER TABLE. Member values are long-horizon (A15b needs months); depth snapshots are short-horizon (A4/A17 replay). Not one number for both.

findings.title: brier_skill_score() has no condition_type filter
findings.root_cause: The query selects our_prob/market_prob/settled_yes with no exclusion at all, so shadow-only rain/snow/hurricane/storm-order and 'between' rows enter the statistic.
findings.evidence: Confirmed callers: web_app.py dashboard and its own tests; no live-trading-gate consumer found. It never had the hardcoded tuple batch-06 unified, so this is not a 'will now disagree' case -- it was always unfiltered.
findings.decision_required: Whether 'between' is excluded. get_station_bias_by_lead deliberately KEEPS it, for reasoning that may not transfer to a calibration statistic.

findings.title: A standalone `py web.py` server never calls load_dotenv, so the dashboard shows code defaults rather than configured values
findings.root_cause: web.py has no load_dotenv call; main.py does at import (~:41). Compounded by config.py binding credentials as module constants AT IMPORT TIME, so import ordering -- not the presence of load_dotenv -- decides whether config is real.
findings.evidence: Reproduced 2026-08-26: a python -c that called load_dotenv() and then constructed a KalshiClient still raised 'API key and private key required', because config.py had already bound the empty values at import.
findings.financial_risk: None directly; an operator may read dashboard values as truth when they are code defaults.
findings.decision_required: Whether a dashboard process should read the same .env as the bot. This is a behavioural change to a live-facing surface.

findings.title: `git restore .` silently resets five learned-calibration files to uncalibrated seeds
findings.root_cause: Five calibration files are force-tracked in git despite data/ being gitignored, so a routine restore reverts them to committed seed values with no warning, and nothing downstream notices it is running on seeds.
findings.evidence: The 2026-08-26 cron run wrote data/seasonal_weights.json via F3 auto-calibration ('seasonal(4) city(0) condition(3) weights written'), so these files change on a normal cadence and a stale restore is a real loss.
findings.financial_risk: Silent reversion to uncalibrated weights on a live pricing path.
findings.decision_required: Where first-run seeds live -- untrack and ship elsewhere, keep tracking with a guard, or leave and document.

findings.title: cmd_walkforward's per-condition Brier silently drops 'between'
findings.root_cause: The per-condition breakdown omits 'between' with no statement of intent.
findings.evidence: Display-only via `py main.py walkforward`; no gate or trading behaviour reads it.
findings.decision_required: Whether 'between' belongs in a per-condition Brier at all. Decide; do not add it reflexively.

findings.title: useData.js's apiFetch has no request timeout, so a hung backend freezes the dashboard instead of degrading
findings.root_cause: No timeout on the fetch, so a backend that hangs rather than errors stalls the whole UI with no indication.
findings.evidence: Filed by batch-61's opus review (F1) as out of scope for that change.
findings.financial_risk: None; an operator may act on a frozen view believing it current.
findings.decision_required: Stale-with-marker vs explicit error state on timeout. Note this frontend has no component-render tests -- logic must be extracted to shared.jsx to be testable.

findings.title: A system alert longer than 256 characters crashes the desktop-toast backend
findings.root_cause: plyer's Windows backend packs the message into a NOTIFYICONDATAW struct with a hard 256-character field; a longer string raises inside the notify thread.
findings.evidence: ValueError: string too long (333, maximum length 256), surfaced as a PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning during batch-68's test run -- i.e. it escapes the notify thread uncaught rather than being truncated or logged.
findings.financial_risk: None; Discord still delivers. It drops the desktop half specifically for the longest, usually most serious, messages.

findings.title: test_trades_placed_below_cap has never exercised the 20-position cap it is named for
findings.root_cause: The fixture never reaches the cap, so the assertion is permanently vacuous.
findings.evidence: Found by an opus review during batch-62 item 1 while tightening a nearby assertion that had been hiding it.
findings.financial_risk: None directly; the position cap is a live sizing gate with no real regression test behind it.

findings.title: test_kelly_property.py has a hypothesis DeadlineExceeded flake under machine load
findings.root_cause: Timing-sensitive property test; the deadline is too tight for a loaded machine.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on unmodified master while regression-testing the isolate_tracker_db change.
